author_or_org: Renjie Liu, Haitian Jiang, Xiao Yan, Bo Tang, Jinyang Li

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: GraphRAG enhances LLMs to generate quality answers for user questions by retrieving related facts from external knowledge graphs.
claims.quote: GraphRAG enhances large language models (LLMs) to generate quality answers for user questions by retrieving related facts from external knowledge graphs.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Current GraphRAG methods are primarily evaluated on and overly tailored for KGQA benchmarks, which are biased toward a few specific question patterns and do not reflect real-world question diversity.
claims.quote: However, current GraphRAG methods are primarily evaluated on and overly tailored for knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) benchmarks, which are biased towards a few specific question patterns and do not reflect the diversity of real-world questions.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The authors propose a complete four-class taxonomy for basic knowledge graph question patterns and use it to create PolyBench, a new GraphRAG benchmark.
claims.quote: To better evaluate GraphRAG methods, we propose a complete four-class taxonomy to categorize the basic patterns of knowledge graph questions and use it to create PolyBench, a new GraphRAG benchmark encompassing a comprehensive set of graph questions.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Existing GraphRAG methods fall short in effectiveness and/or efficiency because they use either a fixed graph traversal strategy or free-form exploration by LLMs for fact retrieval.
claims.quote: With the new benchmark, we find that existing GraphRAG methods fall short in effectiveness (i.e., quality of the generated answers) and/or efficiency (i.e., response time or token usage) because they adopt either a fixed graph traversal strategy or free-form exploration by LLMs for fact retrieval.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Different question patterns require distinct graph traversal strategies and context formation.
claims.quote: However, different question patterns require distinct graph traversal strategies and context formation.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: PolyG is an adaptive GraphRAG approach that decomposes and categorizes questions according to the proposed question taxonomy.
claims.quote: To facilitate better retrieval, we propose PolyG, an adaptive GraphRAG approach by decomposing and categorizing the questions according to our proposed question taxonomy.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: PolyG dynamically prompts an LLM to generate a graph database query to retrieve context for each decomposed basic question.
claims.quote: Built on top of a unified interface and execution engine, PolyG dynamically prompts an LLM to generate a graph database query to retrieve the context for each decomposed basic question.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Compared with SOTA GraphRAG methods, PolyG achieves a higher win rate in generation quality and has low response latency and token cost.
claims.quote: Compared with SOTA GraphRAG methods, PolyG achieves a higher win rate in generation quality and has a low response latency and token cost.
